_comment: PROTOTYPE #482. Hand-transcribed from docs/assets/label-samples/as-captured/ at full 2250x4000 resolution, BEFORE any model was called. Values are exactly as printed: no conversion, no arithmetic, no correction of the label's own inconsistencies. `null` means THE LABEL DOES NOT PRINT THAT ROW - the absent-row instrument.

olive-oil-panel.name: Aceite de oliva virgen extra / Extra virgin olive oil

olive-oil-barcode.layout: net quantity + barcode, barcode rotated 90 deg
olive-oil-barcode.name: Natives Olivenol extra / Huile d'olive vierge extra

indian-paste.layout: ruled table, six languages stacked per row label

notes: The olive oil prints SEVEN rows, not eight: there is no fibre row in either the Spanish or the English prose. docs/assets/label-samples/README.md says its prose 'carries the same eight'; it does not. So fibre is a second absent-row instrument alongside the twelve micros.

The Indian paste's panel is internally inconsistent as printed: 60 g carbohydrate alone is ~240 kcal against a declared 224 kcal, with fat 0 g and protein 0 g. A model that 'fixes' this is wrong. Transcribe what is printed.
The paste's energy header reads '(kj / kcal)' with a lowercase j, and its kJ figure uses a PERIOD (937.21) while the oil's uses a COMMA (3701,13). Both appear in the same set.
The paste's Polish fibre word is printed faint enough to read as 'Bionnik' rather than 'Blonnik'.

EU labels print SALT. The app's panel field is `sodium_content` and the form labels it 'Salt / sodium' in mg, while the OFF mapper fills it from `sodium_100g` (true sodium, salt/2.5). Ground truth records salt AS PRINTED; whether the model, the Worker or the client divides is a contract question for #483, not a thing to hide inside a prompt.
